subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priyanka Shah <pshah@finpay.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes on peak traffic causing poor UX for your chat feature (95th percentile > 1.8s).
- High per-request cost from current managed endpoints when serving streaming responses and embeddings-based reranking.
- Difficulty integrating structured outputs (JSON) reliably from the model for downstream pipelines.

Goals you described:
1) Reduce tail latency to consistently < 1.2s for interactive chat.
2) Replace current pipeline for multi-stage ranking with embeddings + reranking to improve relevant results and cut token costs.
3) Ship an MVP integration in Q2 with predictable latency and monitoring.

What we discussed (product fit / integration notes):
- SDK changes: you’ll use our JS SDK v2.1 (we recommended a small shim to handle streaming + function-calling hooks). I noted the SDK already supports function calling; we suggested a small change to how you serialize call arguments to match your downstream schema.
- Function calling & structured outputs: Redwood can surface function-call tokens as structured JSON with schema validation on-call for deterministic parsing — we recommended the "strict_schema" mode for your use case.
- Streaming: continuous token streaming with chunk annotations so you can render partial structured outputs; this will help UX while preserving ability to reassemble full JSON outputs.
- Embeddings & reranking: we suggested a hybrid approach — coarse embedding search (512-d) followed by a lightweight reranker using our cheaper fast-text model to reduce token usage on full generations.

Attachments: redwood-integration-arch.pdf (high-level arch + suggested SDK shim).

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi to schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week to review the SDK shim and streaming + function-calling examples (Action: Rishi).
- Acme to share a small sample dataset (5–10 queries + expected structured output) so we can prototype reranker config (Action: Alex).
- I’ll add the deal and notes to HubSpot and send a calendar invite for the technical call (Action: Marissa).

If any of this is off or missing, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll proceed with scheduling.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
https://redwood.ai

Date: 2026-02-16T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the convo. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Timeline: Q2 MVP is still the target but the internal product team prefers a soft launch by the end of May. Is the proposed technical deep-dive next week enough to scope work for that timeline?

2) SDK shim: our frontend team uses TypeScript + React. Can Rishi show an example of how streaming partial structured outputs would look in the browser and how to safely reassemble into a final JSON? We also need guidance on error handling when the model emits partial/invalid JSON.

3) Reranking: we liked the hybrid approach. For budget planning, can you ballpark expected per-request token cost improvement (percent) versus our current flow? We’ll share the sample dataset by EOD Monday.

CCing Priyanka since she owns the payment flow and the downstream schema — she may have additional constraints about data retention and logs.

-Appreciate it,
Alex
Product Manager, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-16T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps — Tech deep-dive proposal

Alex — happy to run the deep-dive. Quick technical notes ahead of the call so you know what I’ll demo:

1) Streaming + TypeScript example:
- Will demo our SDK streaming client that emits chunked messages with 3 fields: {chunk_index, content, partial_json_chunk}. In the browser we provide a small helper to stitch partial_json_chunk and run a lightweight validator (Ajv) before handing to your renderer.
- Error handling: demo fallback patterns — optimistic UI with "repair" step (re-request with context) and server-side reassembly + validation to regenerate missing fields.

2) Function calling & strict_schema mode:
- We'll show two modes: permissive (best-effort parsing) and strict_schema (reject and re-invoke with clearer instructions). For deterministic downstream ingestion we recommend strict_schema for your payment confirmations.

3) Embeddings + reranking proposal:
- Proposed pipeline: embed(query) -> ANN search (top 50) -> rerank candidates with fast-text reranker (cheap logits) -> final generation for structured output only for top 3.
- Cost estimate: based on similar customers we see ~30–50% reduction in generation token usage vs always-running full-gen reranker; actual delta depends on pass-through rates (we’ll finalize after seeing sample).

4) SDK change required:
- Minimal shim: a serialize_call_args() adapter to map your internal schema to the function_call payload. I’ll bring a sample patch and sample-config.yaml that you can drop into your pipeline.

Proposed times for the 60-min deep-dive: Tue 2/17 10:00am PST or Wed 2/18 9:00am PST. I’ll attach sample-config.yaml and a short screencap of a previous demo.

Attachments: sample-config.yaml (text/yaml), int-demo-screencap.mp4 (video/mp4, 5MB)

If this looks good I’ll book Tue 2/17 10am for now and send an invite — we can reschedule if that conflicts.

- Rishi
